╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║             RDK-E Middleware QA Dashboard - Docker Quick Reference           ║
║                    Raspberry Pi 4 Deployment Card                            ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ONE-COMMAND SETUP                                                            │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  chmod +x rpi4-setup-complete.sh
  ./rpi4-setup-complete.sh

  → This script handles EVERYTHING automatically!

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ MANUAL SETUP (Step by Step)                                                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  1. Build Image:
     docker build -f Dockerfile.rpi.clean \
       -t rdk-middleware-dashboard:rpi4-clean .

  2. Start Application:
     docker-compose -f docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml up -d

  3. Access Dashboard:
     http://<rpi-ip-address>:11078

  4. View Logs:
     docker-compose -f docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml logs -f

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ESSENTIAL DOCKER COMMANDS                                                    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  CONTAINER MANAGEMENT:
  ├─ docker ps                              # List running containers
  ├─ docker ps -a                           # List all containers
  ├─ docker stop rdk-middleware-dashboard   # Stop container
  ├─ docker start rdk-middleware-dashboard  # Start container
  ├─ docker restart rdk-middleware-dashboard # Restart container
  └─ docker rm rdk-middleware-dashboard     # Remove container

  LOGS & DEBUGGING:
  ├─ docker logs rdk-middleware-dashboard        # Show all logs
  ├─ docker logs -f rdk-middleware-dashboard     # Follow logs (live)
  ├─ docker logs --tail=50 rdk-middleware-dashboard # Last 50 lines
  ├─ docker logs -t rdk-middleware-dashboard     # With timestamps
  └─ docker exec -it rdk-middleware-dashboard bash # Shell access

  DOCKER COMPOSE:
  ├─ docker-compose -f docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml up -d      # Start
  ├─ docker-compose -f docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml stop       # Stop
  ├─ docker-compose -f docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml restart    # Restart
  ├─ docker-compose -f docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml logs -f    # Logs
  ├─ docker-compose -f docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml ps         # Status
  └─ docker-compose -f docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml down       # Stop & Remove

  MONITORING:
  ├─ docker stats                          # Real-time resource usage
  ├─ docker stats --no-stream              # One-time snapshot
  ├─ docker inspect rdk-middleware-dashboard # Detailed container info
  └─ docker volume ls                      # List volumes

  IMAGE MANAGEMENT:
  ├─ docker images                         # List images
  ├─ docker image ls                       # List images (verbose)
  ├─ docker rmi rdk-middleware-dashboard:rpi4-clean # Remove image
  └─ docker history rdk-middleware-dashboard:rpi4-clean # Show layers

  CLEANUP:
  ├─ docker system prune                  # Remove unused artifacts
  ├─ docker volume prune                  # Remove unused volumes
  └─ docker image prune                   # Remove unused images

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ CONFIGURATION CUSTOMIZATION                                                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Edit docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml:

  • Change Port:
    ports:
      - "8080:11078"  # Access at :8080 instead of :11078

  • Add Email Configuration:
    environment:
      SMTP_USER: "your-email@gmail.com"
      SMTP_PASSWORD: "your-app-password"

  • Increase Resource Limits (for 8GB RPi):
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '2'           # Use 2 cores
          memory: 1024M       # Use 1GB

  • Restart Application After Changes:
    docker-compose -f docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml down
    docker-compose -f docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml up -d

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ DATA & PERSISTENCE                                                           │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Docker Volumes (persistent data):
  ├─ app_data           → Screenshots, logs, sessions, device logs
  └─ reference_screens  → Screen validation images

  View Volume Contents:
  docker exec rdk-middleware-dashboard ls -la /app/data/

  Backup Volume:
  docker run --rm -v app_data:/data -v $(pwd):/backup \
    alpine tar czf /backup/backup.tar.gz /data

  ※ Data persists even if container is removed!

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ TROUBLESHOOTING                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Container won't start?
  → docker logs rdk-middleware-dashboard
  → Check if port 11078 is in use: netstat -tulpn | grep 11078

  Web UI not responsive?
  → curl http://localhost:11078 (from RPi)
  → Check container status: docker ps
  → Check resources: docker stats

  High memory usage?
  → Reduce memory limit in docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml
  → docker-compose -f docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml restart

  Volume permission issues?
  → docker exec rdk-middleware-dashboard ls -la /app/data/
  → Check user: docker inspect rdk-middleware-dashboard | grep User

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ KEY FILES                                                                    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Dockerfile.rpi.clean              ARM/ARM64 optimized build file
  docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml      Service orchestration
  docker-entrypoint.sh              Container startup script
  docker-verify-setup.sh            Verify setup correctness
  rpi4-setup-complete.sh            Automated setup script
  .dockerignore.rpi.clean           Exclude execution data from build
  DOCKER_SETUP_GUIDE_RPI4.md        Comprehensive documentation

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS                                                          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  MINIMUM:
  • Raspberry Pi 4 (2GB+ RAM)
  • 32GB microSD card
  • 2 CPU cores

  RECOMMENDED:
  • Raspberry Pi 4 (4GB+ RAM) or Pi 5
  • 64GB+ microSD card
  • Gigabit Ethernet connection

  OPTIMAL:
  • Raspberry Pi 4 (8GB RAM) or Pi 5 (8GB)
  • 128GB+ NVMe SSD
  • Dedicated power supply

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ FINDING YOUR RASPBERRY PI                                                    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Get IP Address (from RPi):
  hostname -I

  Example output:
  192.168.1.100 10.0.0.123

  → Use on another computer at:
     http://192.168.1.100:11078
     http://10.0.0.123:11078

  Find RPi on network (from another computer):
  # Linux/Mac
  arp-scan --localnet | grep -i raspberry

  # Windows (in PowerShell)
  nbtstat -r | Select-String "raspberry"

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ GETTING HELP                                                                 │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Read Documentation:
  cat DOCKER_SETUP_GUIDE_RPI4.md

  Run Verification:
  chmod +x docker-verify-setup.sh
  ./docker-verify-setup.sh

  Check Logs:
  docker-compose -f docker-compose.rpi.clean.yml logs | tail -100

  Verify Setup:
  docker ps
  docker stats
  curl http://localhost:11078
